ClickGui.DisableNotification: Do not print Open/Close messages in chat when the GUI opens or closes.
ClickGui.SoundPitch: Pitch of the click sound; higher is sharper.
ClickGui.GuiSound: Interface sound switch (the only one): button clicks and ClickGUI open/close. Off mutes the whole GUI.
ClickGui.ModuleButtonHeight: Height of each module row; larger spreads the list out.
ClickGui.ModuleButtonWidth: Width of a module row inside the category panel.
ClickGui.CategoryWidth: Width of the whole category panel; the title bar and rows follow it.
ClickGui.CategoryBarHeight: Height of the category title bar (the Combat/Render header).
ClickGui.TextOffset: Vertical nudge for module text; positive moves it down.
ClickGui.TitleOffset: Vertical nudge for category title text.
ClickGui.Alpha: Background opacity of normal (idle) module rows.
ClickGui.HoverAlpha: Background opacity of the row under the cursor.
ClickGui.TopAlpha: Opacity of the top strip of the category title bar.
ClickGui.BackgroundAlpha: Opacity of the panel backdrop; 0 is fully transparent.
ClickGui.TooltipAlpha: Backdrop opacity of the hover tooltip (module info and setting descriptions).
ClickGui.Fade: Fade-in animation when the GUI opens.
ClickGui.Easing: Easing curve used by the fade-in animation.
ClickGui.ScrollAnim: Panels ease toward the cursor while dragged instead of snapping to it.
ClickGui.ScrollAnimLength: Duration of that drag-follow easing; larger feels heavier.
ClickGui.ScrollAnimEasing: Easing curve used for drag follow.
ClickGui.MouseMove: Slight parallax offset of panels following the mouse.
ClickGui.MouseMoveSmooth: How smoothly the parallax follows the mouse.
ClickGui.WalkShake: Panels shake slightly while your character walks in game.
ClickGui.WalkShakeSmooth: Smoothing applied to the walking shake.

ClickGui.Blur: Blur the game behind the panel (needs GPU support).

ClickGui.SnowShape: Snow particle shape: Snowflake or Circle.

ClickGui.Tips: Show control hints in the corner (drag, scroll, SHIFT and so on).

ClickGui.Line: Vertical divider lines on both sides of a module list.

PacketMine.StopDelay: Minimum gap before the next dig starts; too short looks suspicious to the server.
PacketMine.FarCancel: Cancel the target once it leaves Range instead of keeping server-side progress.
PacketMine.StartDelay: Delay before starting to mine, to offset the vanilla rhythm.
PacketMine.Damage: Mining speed multiplier; larger means more progress per tick and faster breaks.
PacketMine.MaxBreak: Upper limit on blocks mined at once; 0 means unlimited.
PacketMine.1.21: 1.21 support: stop sending faked ghost-hand mining packets.
PacketMine.NoCollide: The block being mined temporarily loses collision so you can walk through.
PacketMine.Timing: When to send mining packets: Pre, Post or All.
PacketMine.GrimDisabler: Extra handling to bypass the Grim anti-cheat while mining.
PacketMine.FastBypass: Swing three times in the sky far above the target to blur the one-block-at-a-time pattern. Useful on strict servers only.
PacketMine.Restart: If the block has not broken by the expected time, send an abort + restart pair to recover the progress the server dropped. Has no effect with Instant.
PacketMine.RestartDelay: Extra wait before the restart pair, in milliseconds. Too small reopens every break, too large slows mining down.
PacketMine.GlassDelay: Minimum interval between hits on glass blocks; hitting too fast gets flagged as early break.
PacketMine.Instant: Instant break: skip the progress and fake the server-side validation.
PacketMine.InstantDelay: Minimum interval between two instant breaks in Instant mode (ms), timed from the last STOP.
PacketMine.Wait: Wait while the block has not actually become air yet instead of moving on.
PacketMine.MineAir: Keep mining positions the server has not confirmed yet.
PacketMine.HotbarSwap: Switch items with hotbar keys instead of the inventory.
PacketMine.DoubleBreak: Mine two blocks at once: start the second while the first is nearly done.
PacketMine.AutoSwitch: Automatically put the tool in hand before mining.
PacketMine.Start: When the second block starts, as a fraction of the first block's progress.
PacketMine.TimeOut: Maximum wait for the second block before giving up on it.
PacketMine.SetAir: Set the block to air client-side right after breaking, so the gap shows immediately.
PacketMine.Swing: Play the swing animation while mining.
PacketMine.EndSwing: Swing once more when mining ends.
PacketMine.SwingSide: Who receives the swing packet: All, Client only, or Server only.
PacketMine.UnbreakableCancel: Cancel immediately when the target block is unbreakable.
PacketMine.SwitchReset: Reset the current mining progress when switching items.
PacketMine.PreferWeb: Prioritise breaking the web you are stuck in.
PacketMine.PreferHead: While crawling, prioritise the block above your head.
PacketMine.CheckWeb: Treat webs as solid ground so mining works while webbed.
PacketMine.CheckGround: Check for a block under you and skip mining while airborne.
PacketMine.Smart: Smart check: only mine the block under you when you would actually fall or must.
PacketMine.UsingPause: Pause mining while eating, drinking or drawing a bow.
PacketMine.AllowOffhand: Keep mining with the offhand while using an item.
PacketMine.BypassGround: Disguise the packet timing when mining the block under you, to look less suspicious.
PacketMine.StartRotate: Rotate toward the target block when starting to mine.
PacketMine.EndRotate: Rotate back to your original view when mining ends.
PacketMine.Sync: How long to wait for the rotation to settle before continuing.
PacketMine.YawStep: Step rotation: turn a small amount per tick.
PacketMine.FallFlying: Keep step rotation active while elytra flying.
PacketMine.Steps: Fraction of the remaining angle turned per tick; smaller looks more human.
PacketMine.OnlyLooking: Skip rotation when the block is out of view.
PacketMine.Fov: Field of view used by the OnlyLooking check.
PacketMine.Priority: Rotation priority; higher wins when several modules want the view.
PacketMine.Crystal: Place a crystal in the gap after mining, chaining into crystal damage.
PacketMine.OnlyCev: Only place at head height (Cev), never at the feet.
PacketMine.SpamPlace: Keep trying to place without waiting for server confirmation.
PacketMine.AfterBreak: Place the next crystal immediately after one explodes.
PacketMine.DetectProgress: Watch mining progress and only place once the block is nearly gone.
PacketMine.Progress: Mining progress required to trigger a placement.
PacketMine.Obsidian: Hold this key to lay obsidian as a base.
PacketMine.EnderChest: Hold this key to lay ender chests as a base.
PacketMine.InventorySwap: Pull blocks straight from the inventory.
PacketMine.CheckDouble: Also preview the progress of the second block.
PacketMine.Animation: Progress animation style: Center, Grow, Up, Down, Oscillation or None.
PacketMine.FadeEase: Easing curve when the progress fades out.
PacketMine.ExpandLine: How far the outline expands outward; 0 hugs the block.
PacketMine.StartFill: Fill colour while the block is first being mined.
PacketMine.StartOutline: Outline colour while the block is first being mined.
PacketMine.EndFill: Fill colour when the block is about to break.
PacketMine.EndOutline: Outline colour when the block is about to break.
PacketMine.DoubleFill: Fill colour for the second block.
PacketMine.DoubleOutline: Outline colour for the second block.
PacketMine.Text: Show the mining percentage on the block.

CrystalBot.AutoSwap: How to get a crystal: None, Normal, Silent, or straight from the inventory.
CrystalBot.MinPDamage: Minimum damage to the target required to place.
CrystalBot.Reserve: Safety margin: your HP must exceed MaxSelfDmg + Reserve.
CrystalBot.ExplodeMode: Break timing: Normal, Smart, or Always.
CrystalBot.Remove: Remove the crystal from tracking right after breaking.
CrystalBot.SyncWeb: Sync with AutoWeb: adjust timing when the target is webbed.
CrystalBot.BasePlace: Automatically place obsidian bases under the target.
CrystalBot.BaseMin: Minimum crystal damage required to place a base.
CrystalBot.BaseMax: Maximum self damage allowed when placing a base.
CrystalBot.OverrideMax: Extra allowance on the base self-damage limit for forcing a base.
CrystalBot.BaseBalance: Weigh the HP trade before placing a base.
CrystalBot.OnlyBelow: Only place bases directly below the target.
CrystalBot.InventorySwap: Pull base blocks straight from the inventory.
CrystalBot.DetectMining: Pause base placement while the target is mining.
CrystalBot.OnBreak: Rotate toward the crystal when breaking.
CrystalBot.RotationBypass: Bypass style: Off, ExtraHitbox, PlaceVec or All.

CrystalBot.PlaceTWall: Allow placing through walls, limited by the range below.

CrystalBot.MaxMotionXZ: Maximum horizontal speed used in prediction.
CrystalBot.MaxMotionY: Maximum vertical speed used in prediction.
CrystalBot.SelfPredict: Also predict your own position for a better self-damage estimate.
CrystalBot.SelfPredictTicks: Ticks ahead for your own position prediction.
CrystalBot.GuiPause: Pause while any screen is open.
CrystalBot.RegearPause: Pause while the auto-supply module is working.
CrystalBot.PlacePosMode: Single computes one spot at a time; Double computes two.
CrystalBot.TargetRange: Maximum distance to search for targets.
CrystalBot.WallRange: Range used when the target is not visible.
CrystalBot.Balance: Weigh offence and defence by the HP difference.
CrystalBot.BalanceOffset: Extra HP offset on top of Balance; negative is more aggressive.
CrystalBot.Shrink: Shrink the highlight when the crystal disappears.

CrystalBot.OnlyActive: Only spoof while a target is present.
CrystalBot.InstantBreak: Try to break the crystal the moment it spawns.
CrystalBot.AttackFactor: Extra attack packets sent per break, to improve hit validation.

AutoAnchor.TargetRange: Maximum distance to search for targets.
AutoAnchor.Thread: Run damage and position calculations on a separate thread.
AutoAnchor.InventorySwap: Pull anchors and glowstone straight from the inventory.

AutoAnchor.Fast: Fast placement: continue without waiting for server confirmation.
AutoAnchor.WhenSpamming: Only use fast placement inside the combo loop.

AutoAnchor.SpamDelay: Interval between combo attempts; too low gets rolled back or kicked.

AutoAnchor.ExplosionMin: Minimum damage required to actually detonate.
AutoAnchor.ForceHead: Force a head-position anchor when its damage exceeds this.
AutoAnchor.NoSuicide: Skip when self damage exceeds your HP including absorption.
AutoAnchor.Smart: Skip when self damage would exceed the damage dealt.
AutoAnchor.TerrainIgnore: Ignore terrain obstruction when calculating damage.

AutoAnchor.AssistDamage: Minimum damage required for assist placement.

NoRender.2DItem: Draws dropped items with a simplified render path, saving frames when many items litter the ground.
NoRender.CastShadow: Keeps the ground shadow under dropped items in the fast render path; turning it off saves a little performance.
NoRender.RenderSidesOfItems: Still draws the side faces of flat items like maps and paper; off is cheaper but looks thinner.
NoRender.PotionsIcon: Hides the status effect icons in the HUD corner for a cleaner screen.
NoRender.Weather: Stops rain and snow from rendering and kills the thunder gradient, so bad weather no longer obscures your view.
NoRender.LightsUpdate: Freezes light updates to save performance during chunk loads, at the cost of occasional wrong lighting.
NoRender.ArmorParts: Skips rendering armor model parts, saving performance but making other players' gear invisible.
NoRender.ArmorTrim: Hides armor trim patterns, cutting a bit of rendering work.
NoRender.ArmorGlint: Removes the enchant glint on armor, which helps when everyone wears full enchanted sets.
NoRender.HurtCam: Disables the camera tilt and shake on damage so your view stays steady while being hit.
NoRender.FireOverlay: Hides the fire texture that covers the screen while you are burning.
NoRender.WaterOverlay: Removes the blue water overlay underwater so you can see more clearly.
NoRender.BlockOverlay: Hides the suffocation overlay shown when your head is stuck inside a block.
NoRender.Portal: Stops the purple portal swirl from covering your screen when you stand in a portal.
NoRender.Nausea: Disables the warping and swaying caused by the nausea effect.
NoRender.Blindness: Removes the shrinking, darkening view caused by blindness.
NoRender.Fog: Disables terrain fog so distant blocks stay visible; you see farther but it costs performance.
NoRender.Darkness: Cancels the warden's darkness dimming so caves stay readable.
NoRender.EntityFire: Stops drawing flames on burning entities, keeping fights visually clean.
NoRender.PlayerCollision: Fades other players' models out when they get close, so bodies do not block your view.
NoRender.Effect: Hides the swirl particles from potion effects to cut visual noise.
NoRender.Guardian: Skips the giant elder guardian ghost that flashes on your screen.
NoRender.Explosions: Hides explosion particles, keeping crystal fights clearer and smoother.
NoRender.CampFire: Stops campfire smoke particles from spawning and blocking your view.
NoRender.Fireworks: Hides firework particles so spamming fireworks does not tank your frames.
NoRender.GuiToast: Blocks toast popups such as advancements and newly unlocked recipes.
HoleESP.AirHeight: Display height of the box for air holes with no block below, adjustable from -3 to 3 blocks.
HoleESP.AirYCheck: Only counts air holes at or one block below your Y level, avoiding a screen full of markers.
HoleESP.WallHeight: Display height of the box for holes against a wall, adjustable from -3 to 3 blocks.
HoleESP.SideCheck: Only marks wall holes that have an open side, skipping fully sealed ones.
HoleESP.AirFill: Fill color and opacity used on air holes.
HoleESP.AirBox: Outline color of the box drawn around air holes.
HoleESP.AirFade: Second color of the air hole fill gradient, blending from top to bottom.
HoleESP.UnsafeFade: Bottom color of the gradient used for unsafe, breakable holes.
HoleESP.SafeFade: Bottom color of the gradient for obsidian safe holes.
HoleESP.WallFill: Fill color and opacity used on wall holes.
HoleESP.WallBox: Outline color of the box around wall holes.
HoleESP.WallFade: Bottom color of the wall hole fill gradient.
HoleESP.WallSideFill: Fill color of the landing spot next to a wall hole.
HoleESP.WallSideBox: Outline color of the landing spot beside a wall hole.
HoleESP.WallSideFade: Bottom color of the gradient on the spot beside a wall hole.
Chams.Custom: Replaces the vanilla crystal model with a custom layered one you can color, spin and bounce.
Chams.ChamsTexture: Uses a texture on the custom crystal layers instead of solid color fills.
Chams.Core: Whether the innermost core layer of the custom crystal is drawn, and in what color.
Chams.OuterFrame: Toggles the outermost frame layer of the custom crystal and sets its color.
Chams.InnerFrame: Toggles the middle frame layer of the custom crystal and sets its color.
Chams.Glint: Adds the enchant glint to crystals for a flashier look at a small performance cost.
Chams.Texture: Keeps the vanilla crystal texture; turning it off shows a flat color model with a clearer outline.
Chams.SpinSync: Syncs all crystals to one spin timer so they rotate together instead of independently.
Chams.SpinSpeed: Spin speed multiplier for crystals; 0 is frozen and 3 is the fastest.
Chams.BounceHeight: How high crystals bob up and down; 0 keeps them still and 3 is the biggest bounce.
Chams.BounceSpeed: How fast crystals bob; higher values make the bounce quicker.
Chams.ThroughWall: Renders crystals and the checked entity types through walls, costing more performance the more you enable.
HoverSound.Volume: Volume of the hover sound; 0 is silent and 1 is loudest.
HoverSound.ExpandSound: Plays a sound when a settings group expands or collapses.
HoverSound.ExpandTone: Sound used when expanding a group, choosing between the custom ARC tones and vanilla clicks.
HoverSound.ExpandPitch: Pitch of the expand sound; 0.5 is deep and 2.0 is shrill.
HoverSound.ExpandVolume: Volume of the expand sound, adjustable from 0 to 1.
HoverSound.ToggleSound: Plays a sound when a module is toggled on or off.
HoverSound.ToggleTone: Tone used for the module toggle sound, picked from more than twenty options.
HoverSound.TogglePitch: Pitch of the toggle sound, ranging from 0.5 to 2.0.
HoverSound.ToggleVolume: Volume of the toggle sound, where 0 mutes it.
Timer.HoldKey: Hold this key to switch to the OnKey speed multiplier, release to go back.
Timer.OnKey: Speed multiplier while HoldKey is held, 0.1 to 10, higher is faster.
Timer.TickShift: Banks time while you move and releases it as a speed burst afterwards.
Timer.ShiftTimer: Maximum speed multiplier reached when the charge is full, from 1 to 10.
Timer.Charge: Time needed to fill the charge, 1 to 10000 ms; longer means a bigger stored boost.
Timer.Smooth: Ramps the boost in gradually instead of snapping to full speed, which feels smoother.
Timer.Completed: Color of the percentage readout when the charge is full.
Timer.Charging: Color of the percentage readout while the charge is still building.
NotificationHud.Enable Color: Accent bar color on notifications for modules being enabled.
NotificationHud.Disable Color: Accent bar color on notifications for modules being disabled.
NotificationHud.Info Color: Accent bar color used for plain info notifications.
NotificationHud.Bg Color: Background color and opacity of the notification card.
NotificationHud.Title Color: Text color of the notification title, which shows the module category.
NotificationHud.Msg Color: Text color of the notification body showing the module name and state.
NotificationHud.Text Offset: Fine vertical offset for notification text, from -10 to 10 pixels.
Tips.VisualRange: Alerts you in chat with a chime when a player enters or leaves your view range.
Tips.PopCounter: Announces how many totems each player pops and who dies after popping.
Tips.DeathCoords: Prints your death coordinates in chat so you can go back for your gear.
Tips.ServerLag: Shows a server-not-responding warning when no packet arrives for about 1.4 seconds.
Tips.LagBack: Counts down 1.5 seconds after a position correction so you know you got lagged back.
Tips.ResistanceLevelCheck: Only shows resistance time for Resistance II and above, keeping Resistance I out of the readout.
TargetESP.NurikZapen: Draws a spinning capture marker over each tracked target.
TargetESP.SkipDead: Stops drawing markers on targets that are already dead.
TargetESP.SkipLogged: Drops players who logged out or vanished from the target list.
TargetESP.AutoTarget: Automatically picks the nearest players as targets without manual selection.
TargetESP.TargetCount: How many of the nearest players are tracked at once, from 1 to 10.
FastWeb.OnlySneak: Only speeds you out of cobwebs while sneaking, so normal walking does not trigger it.
FastWeb.AbortPacket: Sends an abort-destroy packet before the stop packet so the break looks normal to the server.
FastWeb.XZSpeed: Horizontal speed kept in Custom mode, 0 to 100 percent; higher means faster sideways.
FastWeb.YSpeed: Vertical speed kept in Custom mode as a percentage, where 100 equals vanilla speed.
Items.HideEmpty: Hides icons for items you have none of, keeping the HUD compact.
Items.E-GApple: Shows how many enchanted golden apples you are carrying.
Items.GApple: Shows how many regular golden apples you are carrying.
HoleFiller.EnemyRange: Only looks for holes to fill around enemies within 0 to 8 blocks of you.
HoleFiller.HoleRange: Radius around each enemy searched for holes, from 0 to 8 blocks.
HoleFiller.SelfRange: Skips holes closer than this to you, 0 to 8 blocks, so you do not trap yourself.
WindJump.ThrowDelay: How long to wait after throwing the wind charge before boosting, 0 to 1000 ms.
WindJump.ForwardSpeed: Horizontal speed during the boost, 0.5 to 20; higher launches you farther.
WindJump.MaintainTime: How long the boost lasts, 10 to 500 ms; longer keeps you flying longer.
Weather.WeatherColor: Color applied to the custom rain and snow particles.
Weather.ExpandSize: Size multiplier for the weather particles, 0.1 to 5; higher is more noticeable.
Weather.Multi: Density multiplier for weather particles, 0.1 to 5; higher means thicker rain or snow.
Spin.Direction: Spin direction: Left turns counterclockwise, Right turns clockwise.
Spin.Direction=Left: Spins counterclockwise, so your view keeps turning left.
Spin.Direction=Right: Spins clockwise, so your view keeps turning right.
Spin.PitchJitter: Pitch shake during the spin, 0 to 30 degrees; higher looks more chaotic.
Tracers.Player: Color of the tracer lines pointing at other players.
Tracers.ShulkerBox: Color of the tracer lines pointing at shulker boxes.
TeleportLogger.Chorus: Marks where a chorus fruit teleport sound came from, staying visible for up to 10 seconds.
Nuker.Sand: Only mines sand and red sand in range, up to the configured number of blocks per pass.
HighJump.Multiplier: Vertical velocity multiplier on jump: 0 cancels it, 1 is vanilla, 5 is the highest.
AspectRatio.Ratio: Forced aspect ratio for the projection; 1.78 is 16:9 and larger values widen your view.
AntiCheat.TrueAttackCD: Resets your attack timer the way vanilla does and only sends hits when the cooldown is actually ready, so servers see human timing.
AntiCheat.MultiPlace: Lets you place several blocks in a single tick, which is faster for tight placements but easier for anti-cheats to flag.
AntiCheat.AttackRotation: Rotates toward the target before swinging so the server sees you actually looking at what you hit.
AntiCheat.PickSwap: Swaps items straight from the inventory with server-side slot changes instead of really moving your held item.
AntiCheat.PriorHotbar: Prefers blocks already in your hotbar, cutting down on inventory swaps that anti-cheats like to watch.
AntiCheat.InteractEntityRange: How far, in blocks, you can still interact with or place around entities; anything past three blocks is often rejected.
AntiCheat.HitBoxSize: Sideways offset used when placing surround blocks: zero sits dead centre, higher values push outward.
AntiCheat.NoBadSlot: Skips sending a hotbar switch when that slot is already selected, removing pointless packets that look like spam.
AntiCheat.Placement: Packet format used for block placement; pick what your server's anti-cheat expects, with Legit being slowest and safest.
AntiCheat.Placement=Vanilla: Vanilla packets: fastest placement of all, but the most obvious to anti-cheats.
AntiCheat.Placement=NCP: Splits the placement action the way NoCheatPlus expects, aimed at older servers.
AntiCheat.Placement=Grim: Aligns rotation and position the way Grim wants: slower, but far less likely to lag you back.
AntiCheat.Placement=Legit: Mimics hand placement with the longest gaps, making it nearly impossible to catch.
AntiCheat.UPDirectionLimit: Under NCP placement, refuses to build against upward faces so the angle never looks invalid.
AntiCheat.AttackSwing: Which side gets the attack swing animation: client, server, both, or none at all.
AntiCheat.AttackSwing=All: Plays the swing on both sides, which looks the most natural.
AntiCheat.AttackSwing=Client: Only swings on your client, so the server never receives the animation.
AntiCheat.AttackSwing=Server: Only sends the swing to the server, keeping your own screen completely still.
AntiCheat.AttackSwing=None: No swing at all: fewest packets, but your attacks end up looking stiff.
AntiCheat.GrimRotation: Sends full position-plus-look packets when rotating, matching Grim's checks so you rarely get lagged back.
AntiCheat.SnapBack: How the view is restored after a rotation: silently next tick, an immediate packet, or not at all.
AntiCheat.SnapBack=Tick: Restores silently on the next tick, which gives the smoothest motion.
AntiCheat.SnapBack=Force: Fires a restore packet instantly so the server sees you snap back right away.
AntiCheat.SnapBack=None: Never restores, leaving your view locked on the target.
AntiCheat.Look: Whether your own camera really turns; disable it to rotate only on the server and keep your screen still.
AntiCheat.LookTime: How long the camera lingers on the target, from zero to one second; too short and the turn looks like a teleport.
AntiCheat.ServerSide: Rotates only on the server while your local view stays put, which is what silent aim needs.
AntiCheat.AlwaysSend: Sends a movement packet every tick even when nothing changed, keeping the server's position from drifting.
AntiCheat.ForceSync: Periodically forces your real rotation to the server so long stretches without turning don't look suspicious.
AntiCheat.InteractRotation: Also sends a rotation packet before opening, placing, or attacking so the action matches where you look.
AntiCheat.DetectDouble: Tracks when the same block gets broken twice in a row so double mining can be spotted.
AntiCheat.DoubleTimeout: Time window for double-mine detection, a zero-to-three multiple of the expected break time; higher is more lenient.
AntiCheat.MinTimeout: Minimum time a double-mine record is kept before it can be cleared, from zero to ten seconds.
AntiCheat.BreakFailed: How long a break may overrun before it counts as failed, tunable from zero to three times the expected duration.
AntiCheat.IgnoreArmorStand: Stops treating armor stands as blockers so placement and mining pass right through them.
Speed.CollideSpeed: Extra push gained per entity you brush against, zero to 0.08; higher moves faster but risks lagbacks.
Speed.Strict: Checks collisions against your exact hitbox without expanding it, which is safer but stricter.
Speed.BoatLongJump: Uses a boat under your feet to launch a jump farther than normal running allows.
Speed.BoatExpand: Extra range for detecting a nearby boat, from zero to one: higher makes the boost trigger more easily.
Speed.BoatSpeed: Horizontal shove from the boat boost, minus two to two; negative values throw you backwards instead.
Speed.BoatJump: Upward bounce applied together with the boat boost, from zero to two blocks.
Speed.InWater: Keeps speeding up while you are in water; turn it off and the boost stops on contact.
Speed.InBlock: Keeps the boost running while stuck inside blocks; disabled by default to stay safe.
Speed.LagTime: How long to wait after a server lagback before resuming the speed boost, up to one second.
Speed.ExplosionsBoost: Converts explosion knockback into forward speed, so bigger blasts send you further.
Speed.VelocityBoost: Adds incoming knockback and velocity packets straight onto your movement speed.
Speed.H-Factor: Horizontal multiplier for the boost, zero to five; one is unchanged and high values feel slippery.
Speed.V-Factor: Vertical multiplier for the boost, controlling how much your jump height gets amplified.
Speed.CoolDown: Minimum gap between two boosts, up to five seconds, so the speed doesn't stack too fast.
Speed.Slowness: Whether slowness is applied to your base speed; disable it to run normally while slowed.
ServerLagger.ArmorPackets: How many armor-swap click packets are fired each tick, from one to ten thousand.
ServerLagger.WindowPackets: Number of fake window click packets sent per tick, between two and twelve.
ServerLagger.OPackets: How many offhand, swap, or slot-change packets go out each tick, up to ten thousand.
ServerLagger.VPackets: Vehicle packets sent per tick from one hundred to ten thousand; only works while riding.
ServerLagger.AACPackets: How many movement packets with impossible coordinates are spammed, aimed at AAC-style checks.
ServerLagger.SlotPackets: How many invalid slot-click packets are sent each tick, up to one hundred.
ServerLagger.IPackets: Interaction packets per tick, up to one hundred, only used by the interact modes.
ServerLagger.MPackets: Randomised movement packets spammed each tick, up to ten thousand.
ServerLagger.CraftPackets: How many crafting requests are repeated for every recipe, up to one hundred.
ServerLagger.SPackets: Number of block-interaction sequence packets, from fifty to two thousand; higher hits harder.
ServerLagger.Empty: In song mode, also throws empty slots so the server has more garbage to process.
ServerLagger.SmartDisable: Auto-disables the module when conditions fail or a packet errors, avoiding pointless spam.
Shader.MaxSample: Maximum edge samples, zero to twenty; higher gives smoother edges at a real GPU cost.
Shader.Divider: Divisor for the sampling step, up to three hundred: larger values tighten the gradient and cut GPU cost.
Shader.Smoothness: Softness of the outline edge from zero to one, hard at the bottom and very soft at the top.
Shader.GlowAlpha: Minimum opacity of the glow outline, invisible at zero and fully solid at 255.
Shader.PulseSize: Width of the pulsing bands, zero to two hundred: larger values make thicker, more obvious sweeps.
Shader.Octaves: Noise octaves layered together, five to thirty; more means finer detail and lower FPS.
Shader.Color1: First layer of the smoke effect, setting the main tint and overall transparency.
Shader.Color3: Third smoke layer colour, adding depth on top of the earlier layers.
Shader.Color4: Final smoke layer colour, shaping the edges and the darker areas.
Shader.Hands: Applies the shader to the items held in your first-person hands as well.
Sorter.Stack: Automatically merges partial stacks of the same item so you free up inventory slots.
Sorter.EditTrash: Opens the item picker so you can edit which items count as trash.
Sorter.Drop: Master switch for dropping; turn it off and nothing is thrown out while sorting continues.
Sorter.Trash: Throws away items on the trash list and leaves everything else untouched.
Sorter.Rename: Treats renamed items as trash too, so odd renamed gear never slips into your inventory.
Sorter.KitExceed: Drops whatever sits in a kit slot but doesn't belong there, keeping the loadout clean.
Sorter.Exceed: Drops anything above the configured amounts, such as crystals, totems, or obsidian.
Sorter.EGapple: How many enchanted golden apples to keep, zero to twelve; the rest get dropped.
SkinFlicker.CAPE: Brings the cape into the flicker so it blinks in and out with your body.
SkinFlicker.JACKET: Adds the jacket layer to the flicker, making the skin look like it's jittering.
SkinFlicker.LEFT_SLEEVE: Flickers the left sleeve on its own so it can desync from the right.
SkinFlicker.RIGHT_SLEEVE: Flickers the right sleeve separately, which makes the desync far more visible.
SkinFlicker.LEFT_PANTS_LEG: Brings the left pant leg into the flicker so the lower body flashes too.
SkinFlicker.RIGHT_PANTS_LEG: Flickers the right pant leg, letting you flash just one leg at a time.
SkinFlicker.HAT: Includes the hat layer so your head covering blinks in and out.
CrystalHurtPeople.CPS: Crystal actions allowed per second, one to thirty-two; higher fires faster but stutters more.
CrystalHurtPeople.FastLayer: Sends extra attack packets and instantly breaks crystals the moment they spawn.
CrystalHurtPeople.StrongLoop: Re-places a crystal in the same tick after breaking, chaining the explosions together.
CrystalHurtPeople.PlaceRate: Places a crystal only every N ticks, one to ten, so higher numbers place more slowly.
CrystalHurtPeople.OnlyBestDmg: Only places when a fresh crystal would deal more damage than breaking the existing one.
CrystalHurtPeople.Rotations: Sends a look packet toward the spot before placing so the server sees you aiming there.
AutoLog.LogOnEnable: Disconnects the moment the module is enabled, giving you a quick escape.
AutoLog.OnPop: Logs you out as soon as you pop a totem yourself.
AutoLog.LowArmor: Logs out when any armor piece drops below five percent durability, before you get deleted.
AutoLog.TotemLess: Disconnects once your totem count falls below the configured threshold.
AutoLog.ShowReason: Prints the logout reason on the disconnect screen so you can see why later.
AutoTrapDoor.CloseDelay: Wait before closing a freshly placed trapdoor, up to half a second; too short and the server may miss it.
AutoTrapDoor.IgnoreNakeds: Skips targets wearing no armor so you don't waste trapdoors on them.
AutoTrapDoor.AntiStandUp: Toggles the trapdoor once after placing so the target can't stand up through it.
AutoTrapDoor.PauseEat: Pauses while you are eating so chewing and placing don't fight each other.
Scaffold.KeepRotate: How long the downward rotation is held after placing, up to three seconds, cutting constant turning.
Scaffold.Tower: Auto-places blocks under your feet so holding jump towers you upward.
Scaffold.SafeWalk: Also stops you from walking off the edge while bridging.
Scaffold.ESP: Draws a ring and a box at the spot where the next block will land.
PopEz.RandomChars: How many random letters get appended to the message to dodge spam filters.
PopEz.SlowSend: Queues pop messages and sends one every few seconds so you don't get muted.
PopEz.CustomMessage: Custom taunt text where %player% becomes the name and %pop% the pop count.
AirPlace.Module: Lets this module handle right-click air placement itself; turn it off to keep only the preview.
AirPlace.GrimBypass: Times the placement packets the way Grim expects, lowering the chance of an illegal-place flag.
AirPlace.Crosshair: Shows a placement box at the empty spot your crosshair points at and lets you build there.
MacePlus.ForwardVelocity: Forward push in forward mode, half to five; higher values launch you farther but are harder to control.
MacePlus.SilentSwitch: Sends slot packets instead of really switching, then restores the original slot right after.
Sprint.InWaterPause: Stops forcing sprint while in water or lava so the server doesn't flag it.
Sprint.BlindnessPause: Doesn't force sprint while blinded, since vanilla wouldn't allow it anyway.
Zoom.ZoomFov: Field of view while zoomed, zero to 130; lower values zoom further, with zero being extreme.
Zoom.AnimTime: Zoom in and out transition time in milliseconds, up to one second; longer feels smoother.
Spammer.RandomWhisper: Whispers a random online player instead of posting in public chat.
Strafe.SlowCheck: When speed and slowness are both active, it skips the speed bonus and uses the slowed value.
CameraClip.NoFront: Switches front third-person to first-person so you never stare at your own face.
ESP.2DOutline: Draws an outline around each box in 2D mode, edges only with no fill.
ESP.2DHealth: Shows a health bar on the left of the box in 2D mode, coloured by remaining HP.
ESP.HighHealth: Bar colour used at 20 HP or above.
ESP.MidHealth: Bar colour used while the target sits between 10 and 20 HP.
ESP.LowHealth: Bar colour at 10 HP or below, so nearly dead targets stand out.
ESP.2DArmorDura: Draws four vertical armor durability bars on the right of player boxes.
ESP.ArmorDuraColor: Fill colour of those armor durability bars, fuller means fresher gear.
ESP.Target: Master switch for boxes around players, dropped items and containers; off leaves only the 2D part.
ESP.EndPortalFill: Fills end portal blocks with colour; off by default.
ESP.EndPortalOutline: Outlines end portal blocks, easier to read together with the fill.
ESP.ItemFill: Fill colour for dropped items, handy when loot is scattered on the floor.
ESP.ItemOutline: Outline colour for dropped items, working with the fill to set the look.
ESP.PlayerFill: Fill colour for player boxes so you can spot people through walls.
ESP.PlayerOutline: Outline colour for player boxes, keeping the edges crisp.
ESP.ChestFill: Fill colour for ordinary chests, easy to spot while looting a base.
ESP.ChestOutline: Outline colour for ordinary chests, separating them from the terrain.
ESP.EnderChestFill: Fill colour for ender chests so they pop out in a storage room.
ESP.EnderChestOutline: Outline colour for ender chests, telling them apart from normal chests.
ESP.ShulkerBoxFill: Fill colour for shulker boxes, easy to pick out while searching storage.
ESP.ShulkerBoxOutline: Outline colour for shulker boxes, making their edges clear.
ESP.CustomName: Shows an item's renamed custom name instead of the plain item name.
ESP.PearlOwner: Labels ender pearls with the thrower's name so you know who sent them.
MaceAura.TriggerDistance: Only actually swings once the target is this close in blocks; farther away it just tracks.
MaceAura.LagbackDistance: Distance threshold in blocks, 0 to 10, for treating a shift as a server lagback.
MaceAura.CooldownTicks: Ticks of cooldown between two smashes, 0 lets you chain them back to back.
MaceAura.TimerSpeed: Game speed multiplier while the timer is on, 1 to 100; higher gets flagged faster.
MaceAura.MaceOnly: Won't swing without a mace in hand; turn it off to hit bare handed.
MaceAura.RenderMode: Normal boxes the real target, Silent draws a fake body at the aim point instead.
MaceAura.RenderMode=Normal: Draws the box on the real player at their actual position, like normal ESP.
MaceAura.RenderMode=Silent: Puts the box on a fake body at the aim point so you seem to be facing elsewhere.
MaceAura.SilentPlayerBox: Box colour for the fake body shown in Silent mode.
MaceAura.OnlyFalling: Only fires while you are falling, ignoring stands and upward jumps.
MaceAura.OnlyAir: Requires you to be off the ground, so nothing happens while standing.
MaceAura.AutoAttack: Master switch for finding targets and swinging; off leaves only the Set routine.
MaceAura.Set: Switches to a stand-still routine that jumps, lags back and then hits.
MaceAura.AttackPull: Raises the hit point half a block in Set mode to reach taller targets.
MaceAura.DelayUntilSwitch: Milliseconds to wait after arming before swapping to the mace.
MaceAura.SetRange: Anchor radius in blocks for Set mode; drifting further restarts the routine.
MaceAura.NoWait: Skips the attack cooldown check and swings early, at the cost of whiffs.
AutoArrow.IgnoreFriends: Skips players on your friends list and never targets them.
AutoArrow.FOV: Largest angle in degrees the bot will rotate, 0 to 360.
AutoArrow.LookAtHead: Aims at the head instead of the nearest body point; better hits, more botlike.
AutoArrow.TPSSync: Scales the fixed draw time by server TPS so laggy servers don't fire late.
AutoArrow.SwitchToBow: Equips a bow automatically and switches back to your old item afterwards.
AutoArrow.ReleaseMode: Release rule: None never, Smart on draw progress, Fixed after a set time.
AutoArrow.ReleaseMode=None: Never releases the arrow; only aims and draws the bow for you.
AutoArrow.ReleaseMode=Smart: Releases once the draw progress reaches your minimum charge.
AutoArrow.ReleaseMode=Fixed: Holds the bow for a fixed number of ticks before shooting.
AutoArrow.FixedTicks: Draw time in ticks for Fixed mode, 1 to 30, where 20 is a full charge.
AutoArrow.MinReleaseCharge: Lowest charge accepted in Smart mode, 0.1 to 1.0; too low flies short.
AutoArrow.PredictTarget: Leads the target by their current velocity so runners still get hit.
AutoArrow.PredictionFactor: Multiplier on that lead, 0 to 5; higher aims further ahead of fast targets.
AutoArrow.CrossbowSupport: Treats crossbows like bows for auto switching and shooting.
AutoArrow.AutoRelease: Releases the mouse button for you once the shot is ready.
Ambience.WorldColor: Tints the whole world's lighting, warm or cold, to change the mood.
Ambience.CustomTime: Locks client time to the value below and drops the server's time packets.
Ambience.CloudColor: Cloud tint that replaces the vanilla colour while enabled.
Ambience.DimensionColor: Overrides sky and fog tint per dimension so every world looks the same.
Ambience.FogDistance: Takes over fog range manually, which makes the two sliders below matter.
Ambience.FogStart: Distance in blocks where fog starts; smaller means it closes in sooner.
Ambience.FogEnd: Distance where fog becomes fully opaque, must stay above the start value.
Ambience.FullBright: Ignores light level so caves and nights stay bright, like permanent night vision.
Ambience.ForceOverworld: Renders the sky the overworld way in every dimension.
Ambience.CustomLuminance: Overrides the light level of every block and reloads chunks when changed.
Ambience.Luminance: Brightness every block renders at, 0 to 15, where 15 is fully lit.
AutoDrop.DropWrongItems: Drops anything that is not the item your kit expects in that slot.
AutoDrop.DropExcess: Also drops extras beyond the count your kit asks for.
AutoDrop.IgnoreArmor: Skips armor so your worn gear is never thrown out as junk.
AutoDrop.IgnoreShulker: Skips shulker boxes so storage boxes are not dumped by mistake.
AutoDrop.OnlyHotbar: Only checks the nine hotbar slots and leaves the backpack alone.
AutoDrop.DropEnabled: Whether items are actually thrown; off means sorting without dropping.
AutoDrop.SortItems: Moves items back into the slots the kit defines before dropping anything.
AutoDrop.InventoryOnly: Only acts while an inventory screen is open, so afk stays quiet.
AutoSupplyPlus.PerferOpen: Prefers opening a shulker already nearby instead of placing a fresh one.
AutoSupplyPlus.Open: Opens shulkers by itself; off means it only handles placing them.
AutoSupplyPlus.MinRange: Skips placement spots closer than this many blocks.
AutoSupplyPlus.Take: Whether it actually pulls items out once the box is open.
AutoSupplyPlus.StealAll: Empties the whole shulker regardless of what you are short on.
AutoSupplyPlus.ForceQuickMove: Uses shift quick move to shift whole stacks instead of slot by slot.
AutoSupplyPlus.PlaceKey: Hold to place and open a shulker right away, release to stop.
AutoReconnect.Rejoin: Reconnects to the last server automatically after you get disconnected.
AutoReconnect.AutoAuth: Sends the login command with your password right after joining.
AutoReconnect.AfterLoginTime: Seconds to wait after joining before the login command goes out.
AutoReconnect.AutoQueue: Clicks the compass for you on queue servers so you can wait afk.
AutoReconnect.JoinQueueDelay: Seconds between queue clicks; clicking faster gets rejected.
AutoReconnect.password: Password string injected into the automatic login command after joining.
AutoReconnect.AutoAnswer: Picks the right answer on queue quizzes from a built-in list.
DropShulkerBox.CheckInventory: Scans the 27 backpack slots for shulkers and drops one when found.
DropShulkerBox.CheckHotbar: Checks the nine hotbar slots too, including the box in your hand.
DropShulkerBox.CheckOffhand: Counts the shulker held in your offhand as well.
DropShulkerBox.DropFullShulkers: Flips it to drop full shulkers and keep the empty ones.
DropShulkerBox.OnlyWhenEmpty: Only touches boxes with nothing inside and keeps loaded ones.
BowBomb.Aimbot: Snaps your aim onto the nearest enemy's head while the bow is drawn.
BowBomb.Spoofs: Fake position pairs sent on release, 0 to 200; more means a wilder arrow.
BowBomb.Minimize: Shrinks the Y offset in the fake packets, quieter but less powerful.
BowBomb.ActiveTime: Seconds after starting to draw during which the exploit can still fire.
Follower.GroundDisable: Switches itself off the moment you land, so you stop following on the ground.
Follower.FallDistance: In Mace mode, blocks of height above the target needed before diving.
Follower.Aim: Keeps your view locked on the target; off leaves your camera alone.
Follower.SendMSG: Prints the reason in chat when it turns itself off.
Quiver.InstantRotate: Only snaps the view straight up for the release instead of holding it.
Quiver.OnlyPress: Only auto-shoots while the hotkey is held, otherwise you draw by hand.
Quiver.ActiveKey: Hold to swap to a bow, draw it and fire the arrow straight up.
AutoPot.SpeedKey: One press throws a Speed potion, pulled straight from your inventory.
AutoPot.StrengthKey: One press throws a Strength potion before a fight.
AutoPot.ResistanceKey: One press throws a Resistance potion to survive when chased.
AutoTK.OnlyFriends: Only spawns copies of friends and ignores enemies.
AutoTK.CopyState: Copies sneaking, sprinting, held items and health onto the double.
Panic.恢复启用: Re-enables every module that panic switched off when you turn it back off.
Panic.白名单: Comma-separated module names that panic never switches off.
Freecam.HSpeed: Horizontal camera speed from 0 to 3, higher flies faster.
Freecam.VSpeed: Vertical speed while holding jump or sneak, tuned separately from horizontal.
AntiCobweb.SafeHealth: Stops the crystal trick once health plus absorption drops to this value.
32KMace.delayUntilSwitch: Milliseconds between throwing the wind charge and swapping to the mace.
AntiVoid.VoidHeight: Scans down to this height; only empty space all the way counts as the void.
AntiEffects.Levitation: Ignores Levitation so potions cannot lift you off the ground.
Crosshair.Thickness: Thickness of the four crosshair lines, 0 to 20.
ViewModel.MainhandSwap: Turning this off makes main-hand item changes appear instantly, without the raise-and-lower equip animation.
ViewModel.OffhandSwap: Turning this off skips the offhand equip animation so offhand changes pop in instantly.
ViewModel.ScaleMainX: Horizontal size of the held main-hand item; 1.0 is vanilla, larger values stretch it sideways.
ViewModel.ScaleMainY: Vertical size of the main-hand item; values above 1.0 make it taller.
ViewModel.ScaleMainZ: Depth of the main-hand item along the view axis; larger values make it look thicker.
ViewModel.PositionMainX: Shifts the main-hand item left or right, in blocks; negative moves it left.
ViewModel.PositionMainY: Moves the main-hand item up or down; negative values sink it toward the bottom.
ViewModel.PositionMainZ: Pushes the main-hand item closer to or further from the camera; negative brings it nearer.
ViewModel.RotationMainX: Tilts the main-hand item forward or back, from -180 to 180 degrees.
ViewModel.RotationMainY: Spins the main-hand item left or right around the vertical axis.
ViewModel.RotationMainZ: Rolls the main-hand item sideways, useful for straightening a tilted model.
ViewModel.ScaleOffX: Horizontal size of the offhand item; 1.0 matches vanilla.
ViewModel.ScaleOffY: Vertical size of the offhand item; higher values make it taller.
ViewModel.ScaleOffZ: Depth of the offhand item along the view axis; higher values thicken it.
ViewModel.PositionOffX: Shifts the offhand item left or right in blocks.
ViewModel.PositionOffY: Moves the offhand item up or down in blocks.
ViewModel.PositionOffZ: Pushes the offhand item toward or away from the camera.
ViewModel.RotationOffX: Tilts the offhand item forward or back, -180 to 180 degrees.
ViewModel.RotationOffY: Spins the offhand item around the vertical axis.
ViewModel.RotationOffZ: Rolls the offhand item sideways for fine alignment.
ViewModel.SwingSpeed: Takes over swing timing; turning it off restores the vanilla swing speed.
ViewModel.Value: How many ticks one swing lasts, 1 to 50; higher means a slower swing.
ViewModel.EatShakeMultiplier: Multiplier for the up-and-down wobble of the hand while eating or drinking. 0 is fully still, 1 is vanilla, 0.1 is the default subtle wobble.
PacketFly.Phase: How you clip: Semi is always no-clip, Full slows you while inside blocks, Off only when already stuck.
PacketFly.Phase=Semi: You can pass through blocks at any time, but the speed is left untouched.
PacketFly.Phase=Full: Clips while inside blocks and cuts speed to about 40 percent, which is harder to flag.
PacketFly.Phase=Off: No clipping of your own; no-clip only turns on when you are already stuck in a block.
PacketFly.NoMovePacket: Cancels the client's own movement packets so only this module's positions reach the server.
PacketFly.BB-Offset: Shrinks the hitbox by 0.0625 blocks when testing for walls, so you count as free sooner.
PacketFly.Invalid-Offset: How far the out-of-bounds packet is offset on Y, 1337 by default so the server sees an illegal spot.
PacketFly.Invalids: Extra out-of-bounds packets sent per move, 0 to 10; more of them makes the server accept sooner.
PacketFly.C-Y: Height below which the horizontal speed disguise kicks in; 0 means only underground.
PacketFly.C-Multiplier: Horizontal speed multiplier below that height, 0 to 2; lower looks more like walking.
PacketFly.Y-Multiplier: Vertical flight speed multiplier, 0 to 2; higher climbs and sinks faster.
PacketFly.X/Z-Multiplier: Horizontal flight speed multiplier, 0 to 2; higher moves faster but flags more.
PacketFly.Jitter-XZ: Alternates horizontal speed between fast and slow ticks to mimic network jitter.
PacketFly.Jitter-Y: Slightly varies upward speed each cycle so your altitude changes unevenly.
PacketFly.Zero-Speed: Freezes your client position entirely; only packets push the server-side you around.
PacketFly.Zero-Y: Zeroes local vertical motion, so the camera stops bobbing up and down.
PacketFly.Zero-Teleport: Sends the confirm packet even before a server teleport id exists, so positions stick faster.
PacketFly.Zoomies: How often the jitter state flips, 0 to 10; smaller flips more often.
AutoTrap.BlockForHead: Which block seals the head slot: obsidian, respawn anchor, cobweb or concrete powder.
AutoTrap.BlockForHead=Obsidian: Seals the head with obsidian, the toughest and most universal choice.
AutoTrap.BlockForHead=Anchor: Seals the head with a respawn anchor, which doubles as a blast trap.
AutoTrap.BlockForHead=Web: Seals the head with cobweb, trapping the target without shielding explosions.
AutoTrap.BlockForHead=Concrete: Seals the head with concrete powder, which hardens once it lands.
AutoTrap.OnlyCrawling: Only traps targets that are crawling or lying flat.
AutoTrap.CheckElytra: Also traps targets wearing an elytra when they are above you or gliding.
AutoTrap.AntiStep: Adds another layer above the head so the target cannot jump out.
AutoTrap.OnlyBreak: Only adds that extra top layer while the target is mining the block above.
AutoTrap.HeadExtend: Fills a 3x3 ring at head height to stop the target peeking out sideways.
AutoTrap.ChestUp: Adds a ring of blocks one layer higher than the chest row.
AutoTrap.OnlyBreaking: Only fills that upper ring while the target is breaking the block above.
AutoTrap.IgnoreCrawling: Skips the chest ring entirely when the target is crawling.
AutoTrap.Legs: Places blocks around the feet so the target cannot squeeze out along the ground.
AutoTrap.LegAnchor: Prefers a respawn anchor for the feet, falling back to obsidian.
AutoTrap.OnlyHole: Only acts on targets standing in a hole with solid blocks around.
AntiSlowFalling.SlowFallingCheck: When slow falling is active, keeps hopping to cancel the sluggish descent.
AntiSlowFalling.YMove: Upward nudge used to cancel slow falling, 0 to 1; higher bounces more.
AntiSlowFalling.JumpTick: Ticks between cancelling hops; 0 tries on every tick.
AntiSlowFalling.ExcludeWater: Stops the cancel from firing while you are in water, so you do not float up.
AntiSlowFalling.NoFallFlying: Leaves you alone while wearing an elytra or gliding.
AntiSlowFalling.NoWeb: Does nothing while you are stuck in a cobweb.
AntiSlowFalling.SpringBack: Sneaks once after a server position correction so it re-accepts your spot.
AntiSlowFalling.BackDelay: How many ticks the crouch lasts, 1 to 20; too short will not recover you.
AntiSlowFalling.SBThreshold: How many position corrections in a row trigger the crouch, 1 to 10.
AntiSlowFalling.SBWindow: Seconds used to count those corrections, 0.5 to 5; smaller triggers easier.
MaceSpoof.BounceInterval: Ticks between each lift packet that keeps the bounce going, 1 to 10.
MaceSpoof.MinFallDist: Minimum fall distance before the packet loop starts, 1 to 50.
MaceSpoof.FakeHeight: Sends a raised position before the hit so the server thinks you fell from above.
MaceSpoof.FakeHeightVal: How many blocks that fake height covers, 1 to 50; higher hits harder.
MaceSpoof.Rubberband: After the hit, throws your position sky-high and back to reset fall distance.
MaceSpoof.RBHeight: Height used by that rubberband sequence, 1 to 50 blocks.
MaceSpoof.FakeFall: Fakes a whole falling path with descending packets for more reliable damage.
MaceSpoof.FakeFallDistance: Total faked fall height, 10 to 500 blocks.
MaceSpoof.FakeFallSteps: Splits the fake fall into this many packets, 5 to 50; more is smoother.
SelfTrap.BlocksPer: Max blocks per tick. SelfTrap now refills feet and chest in one pass, so 4-8 seals a ring at once; lower values feel more human.
SelfTrap.GodMode: Only refills spots mined for longer than the break timer, instead of sealing everything.
SelfTrap.BreakTime: How many seconds a block must be mined before it is placed again, 0 to 3.
SelfTrap.FailedSkip: Ignores positions where mining already failed, so it does not keep replacing them.
SelfTrap.AssumeBreak: Anti-seal: once an enemy has mined your ring past BreakTime, treat that cell as already broken and refill it in the same tick so the gap never stays open.
SelfTrap.SnapRotate: Snap the view straight onto the click face instead of turning step by step. Faster but visibly jittery.
SelfTrap.UsingBreak: Still pop crystals on the landing spot while eating or drawing a bow.
SelfTrap.Center: Teleports you to the exact center of your block on enable and sends the position packet, so you always occupy a single block; recenters automatically if knocked away while standing still.
SelfTrap.HeadKey: Hold this key to seal the head once, without leaving the module running.
SelfTrap.NoBlockDisable: Turns the module off automatically when you run out of obsidian or ender chests.
SelfTrap.MoveDisable: Turns itself off once you move more than one block from where it started.
KillEffect.Lightning: Spawns a lightning bolt on the death spot that only you can see.
KillEffect.LevelUp: Plays the vanilla level-up sound when someone dies.
KillEffect.LMaxPitch: Upper pitch for the level-up sound, 0 to 2; higher is shriller.
KillEffect.LMinPitch: Lower pitch for the level-up sound, 0 to 2.
KillEffect.Trident: Plays the trident thunder sound when someone dies.
KillEffect.TMaxPitch: Upper pitch for the trident sound, 0 to 2; higher is shriller.
KillEffect.TMinPitch: Lower pitch for the trident sound, 0 to 2.
ShulkerViewer.ToolTips: Draws the 27 stored slots right inside the tooltip when you hover a shulker box.
ShulkerViewer.Icon: Overlays the first stored item as a small icon on the shulker box item itself.
ShulkerViewer.Peek: Shows a live preview of what another player is holding in a shulker box.
ShulkerViewer.RenderTime: How many seconds each preview stays on screen, 0 to 100.
ShulkerViewer.Space: Vertical gap in pixels between multiple previews, 0 to 200.
Clip.RotationDelay: Minimum milliseconds between faked position packets, 0 to 500.
Clip.Move: Pushes you half a block forward on enable so you can slip past a block edge.
Clip.MoveIn: Pushes straight along your facing instead of snapping you to the block center first.
Clip.InvalidPacket: Uses +/-1337 out-of-bounds Y packets instead of +/-2; stronger but easier to rubberband.
BreakerEsp.BurrowBox: Outline color for the obsidian block a target is burrowed inside.
BreakerEsp.BurrowFill: Fill color drawn inside the burrow block outline.
BreakerEsp.SurroundBox: Outline color for the obsidian ring a target built around itself.
BreakerEsp.SurroundFill: Fill color drawn inside that surround ring outline.
DeathRespawn.custom-x: X coordinate used after respawn; leaving all three at 0 sends you back to the death spot.
DeathRespawn.custom-y: Y coordinate used after respawn; all three at 0 means the death spot instead.
DeathRespawn.custom-z: Z coordinate used after respawn; all three at 0 means the death spot instead.
Yaw.YawLock: Locks your horizontal facing, snapping to 45-degree steps while Smart is on.
Yaw.PitchLock: Freezes the up-down angle at a fixed value so looking around no longer changes it.
Yaw.Lock: Blocks all view movement, including rotations requested by other modules.
AutoWeb.MaxWebs: Stops laying cobwebs once the target already has this many, 1 to 8.
AutoWeb.FeetExtend: Also webs the ring at foot level, not just the single block, to stop sidesteps.
AntiAFK.AutoReply: Replies with your preset text whenever any chat or system message arrives.
AntiAFK.Reply: The text sent back, and it may start with a command prefix like /r.
PacketEat.DeSync: Keeps resending the use-item packet while eating so server and client timers drift apart.
PacketEat.NoRelease: Cancels the release packet, so the food stays in the eating state.
AntiRegear.SafeRange: Shulkers closer than this are ignored, so you never break the supplies you just placed.
AnimatedGif.WidthSize: On-screen width of the gif in pixels, 50 to 500; height scales with it.
BlockStrafe.AnchorSpeed: Movement percentage while stuck in a block with AutoAnchor running, 0 to 20.
AutoEat.GoldenOnly: Only eats golden apples and enchanted golden apples, ignoring ordinary food.
ElytraFly.InfiniteDura: Re-equips the chestplate every tick and resends the start-flying packet so your elytra barely loses durability.
ElytraFly.Packet: Swaps an elytra from your inventory into the chest slot and flies by packet, so you never need to wear one.
ElytraFly.PacketDelay: Ticks between start-flying packets, 0–20; lower re-sends more often and risks a kick.
ElytraFly.SetFlag: Also sets the local fall-flying flag after the packet, removing the short drop while waiting for the server.
ElytraFly.FireWorkBind: Press this bind to fire a rocket manually for a boost, gated by the cooldown and speed checks below.
ElytraFly.PacketInteract: Uses a packet instead of a real right-click to launch the rocket; stealthier but can desync the client.
ElytraFly.UpFactor: 0–10 climb strength while holding jump; higher rises faster but flags more.
ElytraFly.FallSpeed: 0–10 sink multiplier when not holding jump; higher drops you faster.
ElytraFly.SpeedLimit: Whether horizontal speed is clamped to the cap; turn it off and speed keeps growing.
ElytraFly.MaxSpeed: 0.1–10 horizontal speed cap; anything faster is scaled back down to it.
ElytraFly.NoDrag: Removes vanilla glide drag so your speed no longer bleeds off every tick.
ElytraFly.AutoStop: Cancels movement when the chunk ahead is not loaded, avoiding a rubberband into it.
ElytraFly.AutoStart: Sends a start-flying packet whenever you fall, so you can resume gliding hands-free.
ElytraFly.CheckSpeed: Only fires a rocket when your speed is below the minimum, saving rockets at the cost of pace.
ElytraFly.MinSpeed: 0.1–200 speed threshold that counts as too slow, triggering another rocket.
ElytraFly.Boost: 1–4 extra thrust while holding forward in Boost mode; higher launches you harder.
ElytraFly.MotionStop: In Rotation mode, zeroes your velocity when no direction key is held so you hover in place.
ElytraFly.InfiniteMaxSpeed: 50–170; above this speed in Pitch mode it pitches down to stop runaway acceleration.
ElytraFly.InfiniteMinSpeed: 10–70; below this speed in Pitch mode it pitches up to regain speed.
ElytraFly.InfiniteMaxHeight: -50–360 height ceiling; above it the module forces a downward pitch.
ElytraFly.ReleaseSneak: Sends a release-sneak packet on disable so you do not stay stuck crouching.
InteractTweaks.NoEntityTrace: Ignores entities in front of the crosshair while mining, so a mob in your face no longer blocks the block.
InteractTweaks.OnlyPickaxe: Only ignores entity collision while holding a pickaxe or eating; normal hit detection otherwise.
InteractTweaks.MultiTask: Lets you attack and mine while eating or blocking instead of one interrupting the other.
InteractTweaks.Respawn: Clicks respawn on the death screen automatically, saving one manual click.
InteractTweaks.IgnoreBedrock: Treats bedrock as air when aiming so you can place blocks against it.
InteractTweaks.NoMineAbort: Keeps mining after you release the attack key instead of aborting the block.
InteractTweaks.NoMineReset: Keeps your break progress when switching targets instead of restarting from zero.
InteractTweaks.NoMineDelay: Removes the delay between blocks so the next one starts immediately.
InteractTweaks.NoInteract: Cancels right-clicks on chests, ender chests and anvils unless sneaking, preventing misclicks.
InteractTweaks.SwitchEat: Swaps to a golden apple when you right-click with a sword or pickaxe, then swaps back on release.
InteractTweaks.Sword: Allows the auto golden-apple swap while holding a sword.
InteractTweaks.Pickaxe: Allows the auto golden-apple swap while holding a pickaxe.
InteractTweaks.Reach: Extends block and entity interaction range so you can reach farther targets.
InteractTweaks.BlockRange: 0–15 blocks of block interaction range; higher reaches farther.
InteractTweaks.EntityRange: 0–15 blocks of entity interaction range; higher reaches farther targets.
InteractTweaks.UseDelay: 0–4 item use cooldown; 4 is vanilla and lower lets you spam items faster.
FlatGroundMace.FallHeight: 0.5–15 blocks of faked fall distance; higher hits harder but looks more suspicious.
FlatGroundMace.ResetDistance: 0.05–0.5 block dip before snapping back up, used to trigger the on-ground check.
FlatGroundMace.RequireMace: Does nothing unless a mace is in hand or somewhere in the hotbar.
FlatGroundMace.LockView: Snaps your view onto the target while attacking, securing the hit but fighting your mouse.
FlatGroundMace.SplitStep: 0.1–1.0 block per step upward; smaller is smoother but slower to reach height.
FlatGroundMace.BlinkDelay: 1–20 ticks to hold movement packets before flushing; longer hides more but lags harder.
FlatGroundMace.VMMode: Packet style for Void mace: DoublePacket sends each move twice, Legacy uses the old single send.
FlatGroundMace.VMMode=DoublePacket: Sends every lift position twice, tolerating丢包 better but standing out more.
FlatGroundMace.VMMode=Legacy: Uses the older single send, lighter on packets but one loss ruins the lift.
FlatGroundMace.VMFallHeight: 20–500 faked fall distance that sets the mace damage bonus.
FlatGroundMace.TPCooldown: 1–30 ticks between height jumps; lower lifts you more often.
FlatGroundMace.KeepVelocity: Keeps your current motion during the lift instead of freezing you in place.
FlatGroundMace.AntiAir: Only counts solid ground within six blocks below, so you do not lift off in mid-air.
FlatGroundMace.AttackPackets: 1–10 attack packets per swing; more of them land the hit more reliably.
BAHalo.DynamicFloat: Makes the halo bob slowly up and down as if floating.
BAHalo.FloatRange: 0.01–0.1 bobbing amplitude; higher sways more visibly.
BAHalo.FirstPerson: Draws your own halo while playing in first person.
BAHalo.RaiseReduceOpacity: Fades the halo out as you look up in first person so it does not cover your view.
BAHalo.MinOpacity: 0–100 opacity kept at full look-up; 0 makes it fully invisible.
BAHalo.TrackCamera: Offsets the halo with your camera pitch so it stays visible when you look up.
BAHalo.TrackRange: 0.35–0.5 block radius the halo drifts with pitch; higher moves it further.
BAHalo.PositivePitchLimit: 0–30 degrees cap on how far look-up tilts the halo.
BAHalo.NegativePitchLimit: -30–0 degrees cap on how far look-down tilts the halo.
JumpCircle.OnlyOnGround: Only spawns a ring the moment you land, not when you take off.
JumpCircle.OnlyJump: Triggers only on a real jump; knockback and falls do not count.
JumpCircle.MaxCircles: 1–20 rings kept on screen at once; the oldest is dropped.
JumpCircle.EndSize: 0.5–10 final diameter the ring expands to.
JumpCircle.FadeStart: 0.0–1.0 progress point where fading begins; 1 fades only at the very end.
JumpCircle.RotationSpeed: -5.0–5.0 rotation per frame; negative spins the other way.
JumpCircle.ImageOpacity: 0.1–1.0 texture opacity; higher makes the ring bolder.
JumpCircle.HeightOffset: -0.5–0.5 blocks above your feet; raise it to float the ring.
Blink.PauseModule: Pauses combat and placing modules while blinking so their actions do not get stuck.
Blink.LagbackCheck: Cancels the blink and snaps you back when the server sends a position correction.
Blink.OnlyMove: Holds back only movement packets while attacks and placements still go out.
Blink.Velocity: Blocks explosion and knockback velocity packets so you are not pushed mid-blink.
Blink.LimitPackets: Ends the blink and flushes everything once the queued packets exceed the cap.
Blink.MaxPackets: 0–200 queued movement packets; lower is safer but shortens the teleport.
Blink.Cancel: Press to abort immediately, restoring your position and rotation from the start.
AutoTool.Fish: Turns on the fishing helper, covering auto-cast and auto-reel.
AutoTool.AutoCast: Right-clicks automatically to cast when a rod is held and nothing is hooked.
AutoTool.TicksAutoCast: 0–60 ticks to wait before casting when no bobber is out.
AutoTool.TicksCatch: 0–60 ticks after the splash before reeling; longer is safer but slower.
AutoTool.TicksThrow: 0–60 ticks between reeling in and casting again.
AutoTool.SplashDetection: Only reels when the splash is near your bobber, ignoring other players' splashes.
AutoTool.DetectionRange: 0–60 blocks within which a splash counts as your own.
AutoArmor.Body: Which enchant wins when comparing chestplates: Protection or Blast Protection.
AutoArmor.Body=Protection: Double-weights Protection levels when scoring chestplates.
AutoArmor.Body=Blast: Double-weights Blast Protection levels when scoring chestplates.
AutoArmor.Tights: Which enchant wins when comparing leggings: Protection or Blast Protection.
AutoArmor.Tights=Protection: Double-weights Protection levels when scoring leggings.
AutoArmor.Tights=Blast: Double-weights Blast Protection levels when scoring leggings.
AutoArmor.IgnoreCurse: Treats binding-cursed armor as worthless so it never gets equipped.
AutoArmor.NoMove: Pauses armor swapping while you move and only works when standing still.
AutoArmor.AutoElytra: Prefers putting a working elytra on while gliding and swaps armor back afterwards.
Phase.OnEnable: Throws the pearl the instant you enable the module, no extra key needed.
Phase.PacketMine: Uses the PacketMine module to clear the block you are stuck in, faster and stealthier.
Phase.Paint: Also attacks paintings stuck on you, since they block phasing too.
Phase.DynamicPitch: Computes pitch toward the nearest diagonal instead of a fixed angle, which clips more reliably.
PacketControl.TimerBypass: Locks look packets to one angle with tiny jitter while moving, breaking rotation timing.
PacketControl.PositionPackets: 1–50 position-only packets before switching back to full packets, scrambling the sequence.
PacketControl.PositionSync: Forces a position-carrying move packet every Delay ticks to keep the server in sync.
ArmorHUD.Percent: Shows durability as a percentage instead of remaining points.
ArmorHUD.Background: Fill color of the rounded slot behind each armor piece; transparent hides it.
ArmorHUD.LowColor: Color of the number once durability drops below a quarter, warning you to swap.
Blocker.BevelCev: Fills the diagonal spots above your head with obsidian to deny crystal placements there.
Blocker.OnlySurround: Only adds feet protection when SelfTrap is on, otherwise just guards your head.
DropAntiRegear.DetectShulkers: Finds nearby shulker boxes and opens them to dump their supplies.
DropAntiRegear.DetectRange: 1–8 block radius for finding shulkers; larger finds more but misclicks more.
CrystalPlaceRender.CheckRange: Only draws rings for crystals within range, skipping distant ones for performance.
CrystalPlaceRender.TranslateDistance: 0.1–5 blocks the ring drifts outward in Translate mode.
AntiWeak.OnlyCrystal: Only handles attack packets aimed at crystals, leaving player hits alone.
PlayerModel.ModelSize: 5–200 on-screen model size, which also sets the HUD box.
FastFall.NoLag: Uses a gentler downward push so you fall fast without rubberbanding.
ChestStealer.PerTick: 1–10 stacks moved per action; higher empties the container faster.
Fov.ItemFov: 30–170 FOV for the held item, tuned separately from the world FOV.
TwoDESP.Settings: Which panel page is open: Setting for toggles, Target for entity filters, Color for palettes.
TwoDESP.Settings=Setting: Switches to the options page where health bars, armor durability, effects and item labels live.
TwoDESP.Settings=Target: Switches to the target page where you pick which entity types get boxes.
TwoDESP.Settings=Color: Switches to the color page for box, health bar and text colors.
TwoDESP.Armor Dura Color: Color of the armor durability bars drawn as four strips on the right of each player box.
TwoDESP.High Health Color: Bar color when the target sits at 20 health or above, green by default.
TwoDESP.Mid Health Color: Bar color while health is between 10 and 20, yellow by default.
TwoDESP.Low Health Color: Bar color once health drops to 10 or below, red by default.
TwoDESP.renderHealth: Draws the target health bar so you can read remaining HP from afar.
TwoDESP.Armor Dura: Shows durability strips for all four armor pieces beside the player box.
TwoDESP.draw Item Name: Draws the item name above dropped item entities on the ground.
TwoDESP.draw Item Count: Appends the stack size after the item name, like x32.
TwoDESP.Item Count Color: Color of the stack count digits after the item name, yellow by default.
TwoDESP.Item Name Color: Text color of dropped item names, light purple by default.
TwoDESP.CustomFont: Renders effect timers with the client font for a cleaner, more consistent look.
TwoDESP.PlayersBox: Box color for regular unknown players, orange-yellow by default.
TwoDESP.FriendsBox: Box color used for friends, green by default.
TwoDESP.CrystalsBox: Box color for end crystals, cyan by default.
TwoDESP.CreaturesBox: Box color for animals and water creatures, matched by spawn group.
TwoDESP.MonstersBox: Box color for hostile monsters, red by default.
TwoDESP.AmbientsBox: Box color for ambient mobs such as bats and squid.
TwoDESP.OthersBox: Box color for entities that fall outside the other categories.
ChunkESP.Chunks-Distance: Render distance for chunk marks in chunks, 6–1024; larger values cost more FPS.
ChunkESP.RenderHeight: Y offset of the chunk overlay, -112–319, to lift or sink the mark to ground level.
ChunkESP.PaletteExploit: Compares block palettes to tell new chunks from old, the most accurate check.
ChunkESP.BeingUpdated: Flags chunks the server is resending so updates are not mistaken for fresh terrain.
ChunkESP.OverworldOldChunks: Uses deepslate and azalea style blocks to spot old-generation overworld chunks.
ChunkESP.NetherOldChunks: Uses ancient debris and blackstone to spot old-generation nether chunks.
ChunkESP.EndOldChunks: Reads the end biome palette to flag chunks generated before the update.
ChunkESP.LiquidExploit: Counts flowing liquid updates as new chunks; more sensitive but noisier.
ChunkESP.blockUpdateExploit: Marks a whole chunk on any single block update, used with Normal mode to filter false positives.
ChunkESP.WorldLeaveRemove: Clears stored chunks on disconnect or world leave so nothing lingers into the next session.
ChunkESP.RemoveRenderDist: Drops records beyond the render distance to save memory on long trips.
ChunkESP.New: Fill color for chunks judged freshly generated, translucent red by default.
ChunkESP.BlockExploit: Fill color for chunks flagged by the block-update exploit, translucent blue by default.
ChunkESP.Old: Fill color for old chunks, translucent green by default.
ChunkESP.BeingUpdatedColor: Fill color for chunks the server is currently resending.
ChunkESP.OldVersion: Fill color for chunks left from older world generation, yellow-green by default.
Velocity.IgnorePearlLag: Ignores rubberband packets right after a pearl so knockback cancel keeps working.
Velocity.PhaseTime: How long after a pearl rubberbands stay ignored, 0–1000 ms.
Velocity.FlagInWall: Also triggers while stuck inside blocks, rescuing knockback when clipped into walls.
Velocity.WhilePushOut: Still sends the packet while the server pushes you out of blocks; stronger but easier to rubberband.
Velocity.Static: Only triggers while standing still; knockback is left alone while moving.
Velocity.CancelAll: Cancels the whole velocity packet outright; maximum effect but the highest rubberband risk.
Velocity.Horizontal: Percent of horizontal knockback kept, 0 removes it and 100 stays vanilla.
Velocity.Vertical: Percent of vertical knockback kept, 0 kills the pop-up and 100 is vanilla.
Velocity.WhileLiquid: Keeps handling knockback while in water or lava.
Velocity.NoClimb: Disables ladder and vine climbing so pushes cannot drag you upward.
Velocity.NoWaterPush: Stops flowing water from shoving you around while you stand in it.
Velocity.NoEntityPush: Stops other entities from pushing you, keeping your footing in close fights.
Velocity.NoBlockPush: Stops blocks from ejecting you when you clip into them.
Velocity.NoFishBob: Ignores the fishing rod tug so a hooked line cannot drag you off spot.
NameTag2D.MinScale: Floor for the nametag scale, 0.1–1.0, so distant tags stay readable.
NameTag2D.Scaled: Distance shrink strength, 0–2; higher makes far tags shrink faster.
NameTag2D.God: Prefixes GOD when the player has slowness, marking god-mode abusers.
NameTag2D.TotemPops: Appends how many totems that player has already popped.
NameTag2D.Enchants: Labels enchantment shorthand and level beside armor icons, like P4.
NameTag2D.Turtle: Shows a resistance icon and timer when the player is splashed with turtle master.
NameTag2D.FriendColor: Name color used for friends, bright green by default.
NameTag2D.ArmorHeight: Vertical position of the armor icon row, -10 to 10, to dodge the name.
NameTag2D.ArmorScale: Armor icon size, 0.1–2.0; larger icons take more horizontal room.
FastProjectile.Packets: How many position packets are spammed on release, 1–500; faster but kick-prone.
FastProjectile.ChargeDelay: Cooldown between speed bursts, 0–3 s, to avoid drawing attention.
FastProjectile.Bows: Applies to bows, speeding the arrow up the moment you release a full draw.
FastProjectile.Crossbows: Applies to crossbows so their bolts get the same speed boost.
FastProjectile.Tridents: Applies to tridents, making thrown ones travel faster.
FastProjectile.EnderPearls: Applies to ender pearls so they reach the landing spot sooner.
FastProjectile.Snowballs: Applies to snowballs, boosting them with the same trick.
ItemCounter.Spacing: Gap between the totem and crystal lines, 0–20 pixels.
ItemCounter.ShowIcon: Draws the item icon before the count; wider but instantly readable.
ItemCounter.TotemColor: Base color for the totem count and the start of the pulse gradient.
ItemCounter.TotemColor2: Second color of the totem pulse gradient, only used in pulse mode.
ItemCounter.CrystalColor: Base color for the crystal count and the start of the pulse gradient.
ItemCounter.CrystalColor2: Second color of the crystal pulse gradient, only used in pulse mode.
ItemCounter.PulseCounter: Steps in the pulse cycle, 1–50; higher keeps both lines closer in color.
BreakESP.FriendBox: Outline color used when a friend is breaking, blue by default.
BreakESP.FriendFill: Fill color when a friend is breaking, translucent blue.
BreakESP.Second: Also draws a second player's break progress on the same block, marked white.
BreakESP.SecondBox: Outline color for the second breaker's progress, white by default.
BreakESP.SecondFill: Fill color for the second breaker's progress, translucent white by default.
AutoEnderChest.TargetShulkers: How many shulkers to pull from the ender chest, 0–36; stops once reached.
AutoEnderChest.PreferCrystal: Temporarily disables auto crystal while running to avoid block and input conflicts.
AutoEnderChest.StoreItems: When the inventory is full, dumps junk into the chest to free slots first.
AutoEnderChest.StoreCount: Max items stored into the chest, 1–36, so gear is not dumped by mistake.
SkyColor.ThickFog: Enables thick fog in Flat and End modes so distance fades sooner.
SkyColor.ForceSky: Forces a normal sky dome so dimensions like the nether can show color too.
SkyColor.Overworld: Whether custom sky and fog colors apply in the overworld.
SkyColor.Nether: Whether custom sky and fog colors apply in the nether.
Punctuation.ClearTime: How long the ground beacon mark stays, 0–100 s, before it vanishes.
Punctuation.EnemySpot: Hold this key to mark the block under your crosshair as a beacon.
Punctuation.EncryptKey: AES key for decrypting teammate coordinate messages; must match theirs.
PhaseESP.BevelDistance: Reach check for diagonal blocks, 0–1; smaller marks only diagonals near your feet.
PhaseESP.SemiSafeFill: Fill color for semi-safe blocks that are solid but not sitting on bedrock.
PhaseESP.SemiSafeBox: Outline color for semi-safe blocks, yellow by default.
CevBreaker.Top: Allows obsidian directly above the head before blowing it up.
CevBreaker.Bevel: Allows obsidian on the four diagonals to cover more blast spots.
FakePlayer.Record: Starts recording your movement and view; toggling it on clears old data.
FakePlayer.Play: Loops the recorded path on the fake player for combo practice.
MotionCamera.NoFirstPerson: Skips camera smoothing in first person for a snappier view.
MotionCamera.FirstPersonSpeed: First person follow speed, 0–1; higher is tighter, lower lags behind.
AutoMend.OnlyBroken: Throws bottles only when mending armor is actually damaged.
ArmorPreserve.Threshold: Unequips armor once durability falls under this percent, 1–100.
FastSwim.DownFactor: Sink speed when no key is pressed, 0–1; 0 hovers in place.
IQBoost.IQ: Only changes the IQ number shown on the module, 0–1000, with no gameplay effect.
KillThunder.Amount: Total lightning bolts dropped around a kill, 1–20.
BlockLag.RotateMode: How to rotate when placing blocks and hitting crystals: none, snap instantly, or step gradually.
BlockLag.RotateMode=None: Never rotates and places using your current view.
BlockLag.RotateMode=Normal: Snaps your view onto each block, then snaps back.
BlockLag.RotateMode=Bypass: Pre-aims once, then faces each block to dodge common rotation checks.
BlockLag.RotateMode=Grim: Sends no rotation packets and relies on the server not checking facing.
BlockLag.RotateMode=Yawstep: Splits the turn across several ticks so it reads like human aim.
BlockLag.YawStepSteps: Share of yaw turned per packet in Yawstep mode; 0.1 is smooth, 1.0 snaps in one tick.
BlockLag.MoveLagMode: Which lag-back packet pulls your server position in when the head-blocked case needs a fake move.
BlockLag.cancuiHeight: Downward offset in blocks for that lag-back; negative values move up to slip past head blocks.
BlockLag.WebTime: Milliseconds to wait after leaving a cobweb before acting, so packets aren't wasted inside it.
BlockLag.AntiLag: Only acts when a solid block sits under your feet, avoiding lag-backs while airborne.
BlockLag.CancelBlink: Stops working while Blink is on, so held position packets don't break the placement.
BlockLag.AutoCenter: Automatically walks you to the exact center of the hole before placing.
BlockLag.SingleBlock: Only runs when you're not inside a block; if clipped into one, the attempt is skipped.
BlockLag.HeadFill: Also fills the two blocks above your head so crystals can't be dropped from above.
BlockLag.2QE_: Uses ender chests for the head fill, saving obsidian but costing more and standing out.
BlockLag.NoSelfPos: Skips the block directly under your feet and never places there.
BlockLag.FakeMove: Sends fake movement packets to slide you sideways when you can't fit, then keeps placing.
BlockLag.AllowCenter: When the fake move finds nowhere to stand, allows walking straight to a neighboring center.
BlockLag.PreCorrect: Size of the first correction step in the fake move; 0 disables it, larger jumps closer.
BlockLag.MoveDis: Distance moved per packet in the main loop; smaller values send more packets and look legit.
BlockLag.MoveDis2: Step size in the closing phase of the fake move, used to clear the last bit of distance.
BlockLag.SmartDistance: Minimum distance in blocks for the spot it picks; larger values teleport you farther away.
